---
title: Setup
description: What you need before the session, how to choose the browser or the command line, and what to do if something is missing.
---

Each exercise has a browser route and a command-line route. The browser route needs no software, and neither route needs homework. For both routes, you need three things.

| You need | Why | If you do not have it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A laptop with a current desktop browser | The GitHub interface hides parts of the menus on a phone. | Share a laptop with a neighbour. |
| A GitHub account | Every exercise creates something in your account. | Create one at the start (allow 10 minutes), or work in a pair. |
| Two-factor authentication that works on the day | GitHub asks for a second factor at sign-in. | Bring the device or the recovery codes that you use for GitHub. |

## Create a GitHub account

If you have no account yet, create it before the session if you can.

1. Open [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup).
2. Use an e-mail address that you can open during the session.
3. Choose a username that you are comfortable to show in public. Your username appears on every repository and Issue.
4. Confirm the e-mail address.
5. Set up two-factor authentication when GitHub asks for it.

The free plan (GitHub Free) is sufficient. Students can also apply for [GitHub Education](https://education.github.com/), but the workshop does not need it.

## Choose your path

Before X1, decide how you work. You can change the decision later.

| Path | Who it is for | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Solo, public** | Default | Your exercise repository and Project are public. They contain only synthetic data. |
| **Solo, private** | You do not want public activity under your name. | Select **Private** for the repository and the Project. All exercises work the same way. |
| **Pair** | You have no account, or you prefer to work together. | One person owns the repository and the Project and gives the partner access to both. You review each other's pull requests in X4. |

### Work in a pair

Repository access and Project access are separate. Access to the repository does not give access to the Project. The owner gives both.

1. In X1, open the repository and click **Settings**.
2. Under **Access**, click **Collaborators**, then **Add people**.
3. Search for your partner and add them. Your partner accepts the invitation.
4. In X3, open the Project. Click **…** (top right), then **Settings**.
5. Click **Manage access**. Under **Invite collaborators**, search for your partner.
6. Select the role **Write** and click **Invite**.

A partner without an account works on the owner's laptop. Swap the keyboard at each exercise.

## Choose your route {#routes}

Each exercise reaches the same result on two routes. The **path** above decides what you share. The **route** decides how you work.

| Route | You need | Choose it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Browser** | A current desktop browser | GitHub is new to you, or you cannot install software on your laptop. |
| **Command line** | git, gh (the GitHub command-line tool), a terminal, and a text editor | You know some command line, or you want to learn the workflow for your own computer. |

Each exercise shows the routes as two tabs: **Browser** and **Command line**. When you select a tab, all tabs on the page switch together. A step without a usable command says **Browser only**. Both routes change the same repository on GitHub, so you can change the route at any step. The [cheat sheet](cheat-sheet.qmd#version-control) explains what git does.

## Prepare the command line {#command-line-route}

Do this before the session. Allow 15 minutes. If a step fails, use the browser route. You lose nothing.

1. Install git from [git-scm.com/downloads](https://git-scm.com/downloads). On Windows, the installer also installs **Git Bash**.
2. Install gh from [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/). The instructor tested the exercises with gh 2.102.0. Install this version or a later one.
3. Open a terminal. On Windows, open Git Bash, because the commands on this site use its syntax.
4. Check both tools. Each command prints a version number.

   ```bash
   git --version
   gh --version
   ```

5. Sign in to GitHub in the browser window that gh opens. The option `--scopes project` gives gh access to Projects.

   ```bash
   gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --scopes project
   ```

6. Let git use the sign-in of gh when it sends commits to GitHub:

   ```bash
   gh auth setup-git
   ```

7. Set the name and the e-mail address that git writes into each commit. Use your no-reply address from **Settings → Emails** on GitHub.

   ```bash
   git config --global user.name "Your Name"
   git config --global user.email "ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com"
   ```

8. Check the sign-in. The line "Token scopes" includes `project`.

   ```bash
   gh auth status
   ```

If you signed in to gh before, add the access to Projects with `gh auth refresh -s project`.

Each commit shows its name and e-mail address to everyone who can see the repository. The no-reply address keeps your private address private ([Setting your commit email address](https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/setting-up-and-managing-your-personal-account-on-github/managing-email-preferences/setting-your-commit-email-address)).

You also need a text editor for Markdown files. Any editor that saves plain text works, for example Visual Studio Code.

### Command-line problems {#command-line-problems}

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "command not found: gh" or "command not found: git" | The tool is not installed, or the terminal opened before the installation. | Open a new terminal. If the error stays, install the tool again. |
| "fatal: not a git repository" | The terminal is not in the project folder. | Run `cd projm-thesis`. |
| gh reports that the token is missing the scope `project`. | You signed in without access to Projects. | Run `gh auth refresh -s project`. |
| `git push` asks for a user name and a password. | git does not use the sign-in of gh. | Run `gh auth setup-git`. Then push again. |
| `git push` is rejected with "fetch first". | GitHub has commits that your computer does not have, for example from the browser route. | Run `git pull --rebase`. Then push again. |
| An editor opens in the terminal. | git asks for a message. | In nano, press `Ctrl`+`X`. In vim, type `:wq` and press `Enter`. |
| Another error | — | Do the step in the browser. Both routes reach the same state. |

::: {.callout-important}
## Synthetic data only

Do not put real personal data, unpublished research data, or third-party material into an exercise repository. The workshop gives you a synthetic dataset. For your real thesis, start with a **private** repository and a **private** Project. See [Transfer to a private thesis](after.qmd#private-thesis).
:::

## What to open on the day

- This website. If GitHub is new to you, read the [cheat sheet](cheat-sheet.qmd) before the session.
- The [template](https://github.com/maehr/open-research-data-template) that you start from in X1.
- The [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) and the [example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis), for comparison.
